_doc: GENERATED by tools/derive_hardscrabble_1812.py from data/terrain/1812_hardscrabble_readings.json and the committed river lines it names - do not hand-edit; --check re-derives it. Lee's Place (later Hardscrabble) is placed here as a STATION and a REACH of the South Branch's north-west bank, never as a point claimed for the cabin. T-2503 builds on this reach, and T-2502 carries the 1812 ground down to it.

river.note: Along the old channel's west bank and the main stem's south bank from the 1812 outlet, across the forks window on a straight chord, then down the South Branch's centre. The South Branch is Wright 1834 to N -2110, then Rees 1849 to 40 m below the box floor, then T-2501's Rees 1849 trace to the canal.

bridgeport.note: Where the canal opens into the river's south fork on Rees & Rucker 1849. That is the trace's last vertex, picked by eye to +/-8 px (about 16 m).

forks.note: The trace's vertex nearest the picked junction of the west and south forks.

site.station: half a mile below Bridgeport by river, on the north-west bank
site.uncertainty: The reach is the stretch of bank that Hubbard's 'about half a mile' allows: 0.25 to 0.75 mi below Bridgeport. Beyond it, the Rees 1849 georeference carries 25.0 m RMS (35.7 m worst), and the sheet is 37 years after the farm.
site.note: The station is the river point half a mile downstream of the canal's mouth, carried across to the north-west bank along the trace's own normal. The field lay back from that bank, and the cabin's place on it is T-2503's.

tests.says: about three miles from the garrison
tests.reading: Read as a straight line. The river route from the fort is printed beside it and is longer, because it goes round by the forks.

tests.says: some four miles southwest of the fort ... about where ... the canal opens into that stream
tests.reading: Currey's point is the canal's mouth itself. His four miles south-west of the fort agrees with it (the bearing is the compass's south-west quadrant), so this placing and Hubbard's differ by Hubbard's half mile, measured along the river. That gap is the disagreement, and 'about where' is Currey's own hedge.

tests.says: some four miles from the mouth of the river
tests.reading: Measured along the river from the 1812 outlet, up the old channel, along the main stem and down the South Branch. The chord across the forks window makes this a slight under-measure, so the true river distance is a little longer still. By river, four miles from the mouth does not reach the site, nor Currey's own canal mouth: it falls at the box floor, about a mile short of both. In a straight line from the outlet, the site is under three miles and the canal's mouth about three and a half. So the caption's four miles fits neither measure of either point, and the reading most like it is the text's own four miles from the fort, repeated with a different starting point. This is recorded as a disagreement and not resolved.

tests.says: on the northwestern side of the South branch, near its forks
tests.reading: The site is on the north-west bank by construction, because it is Hubbard's 'north side', and this is that same bank. 'Near its forks' sets no distance; the figure above is how far from the traced forks the station lies.

agreement.disagreement: Currey's text puts the farm AT the canal's mouth, and Hubbard puts it half a mile below. The reach adopted is Hubbard's. It comes no closer to the canal than a quarter mile, so Currey's point lies outside it. Currey's caption measures four miles from the mouth, and by river that falls about a mile short of both points. Heald's three miles from the garrison, and Moses and Kirkland's north-west bank near the forks, both agree with the adopted site. No placing puts the farm on the other bank.
